assertionResults.reason: The isolated current-branch daemon returned explicit errors for malformed and missing session targets (401 missing_token, 400 invalid_name, 404 session_not_found) and the raw gateway-wrapped dot-segment traversal probe returned 400 malformed_path instead of routing to /v1/sessions. This shows the current branch behaves correctly and the earlier 127.0.0.1:7788 result was stale shared-gateway evidence, not a current-branch failure.

frictions.description: A first isolated daemon launch under the default macOS temp path exceeded the UNIX socket pathname limit.
frictions.resolution: Switched the validator to a shorter /tmp-backed HOME so the current-branch daemon socket path stayed within system limits.

frictions.description: The isolated daemon reported the optional auth server port 7790 was already in use by another process.
frictions.resolution: Continued with direct daemon-socket and gateway probes because VAL-ENV-006 only exercises session/runtime and control-plane route guards, which were live on the isolated socket and gateway port.

commands.observation: The isolated current-branch daemon socket responded 200, confirming probes hit the temp-HOME daemon rather than the shared global gateway.
Unauthenticated control-plane access returned 401 with explicit missing_token guidance.
Malformed session identifiers stayed explicit with 400 invalid_name validation.
Missing session targets returned 404 session_not_found instead of falling through to another route.
The raw dot-segment traversal probe returned 400 with malformed_path on the isolated current-branch daemon gateway.
Focused daemon and gateway regression tests were rerun to support the live probe results.

summary: Tested 1 assertion: VAL-ENV-006 passed on an isolated current-branch daemon. The temp-HOME daemon and non-shared gateway returned explicit missing_token, invalid_name, and session_not_found errors, and the raw traversal probe returned malformed_path, so the earlier 200 response from the shared 127.0.0.1:7788 gateway was stale evidence from the wrong daemon surface.
